name: Claude Code
recommended: Complex multi-file refactors and architectural changes
description: Claude Code is Anthropic's terminal-based coding agent with deep reasoning capabilities, subagent delegation, and a plugin system. It excels at complex multi-file refactoring and architectural changes, featuring the highest SWE-bench score in its class (88.6%). Pricing ranges from $20-200/mo with usage-based billing. No local-only mode available.

name: Hermes Agent
recommended: Automated workflows, scheduled tasks, and multi-model setups
description: Hermes Agent is a full-featured open-source terminal coding agent with built-in cron scheduling, multi-provider routing, subagent delegation, and a console dashboard. It supports background tasks, memory persistence, skills system, and MOA (Mixture of Agents) orchestration. Free with BYO API keys. Designed for automated workflows, scheduled tasks, and complex multi-model setups.

name: Cursor
recommended: Everyday interactive development and quick edits
description: Cursor is an AI-native IDE built as a VS Code fork with deep AI integration. It features the Composer for multi-file editing, background agents for parallel tasks, and fast inline editing. SWE-bench score of 91.2%. Pricing $20-200/mo with usage-based billing. No cron/scheduling. Closed source with VS Code fork lock-in.

name: OpenCode
recommended: Open-source alternative with flexible provider choice
description: OpenCode is a skill-driven terminal coding agent with multi-provider support and a slash-command workflow system. It executes SKILL.md files for repeatable coding tasks. SWE-bench score of 88.0%. Free and open source with BYO API keys. Note: project is archived with no active development. No vision support or subagents.

name: Mimo Code
description: Mimo Code is an OpenCode fork that adds vision support and reasoning model integration while maintaining the skill-driven execution model. Free and open source with BYO API keys. Active development with a smaller community than OpenCode. No subagents or cron scheduling.

name: Kilo Code CLI
recommended: Quick code tasks and lightweight terminal work
description: Kilo Code is a lightweight terminal coding agent designed for quick AI-assisted tasks. It features fast startup, usage stats tracking, auto-update, and a console dashboard. Free with BYO API keys. No background tasks, git integration, or plugin system. Best for quick code tasks and lightweight terminal work.

name: pi.dev
description: pi.dev is a terminal agent focused on long-running knowledge-backed agents with persistent knowledge graphs, scheduled tasks, and background agents. Free with BYO API keys. Features cron scheduling and subagent support. No git integration or plugin system. Small community. Best for knowledge-intensive long-running agent tasks.

name: Oh My Pi
description: Oh My Pi is a hash-anchored terminal coding agent with the largest model catalog, vision support, browser automation, LSP integration, and subagent system. Free with BYO API keys. Daily releases (v16+) mean rapid feature iteration but can break configs. No built-in cron. Less polished TUI than commercial alternatives. Best for model experimentation and multi-model workflows.

name: Gitlawb Zero
recommended: Privacy-focused developers who want full control
description: Gitlawb Zero is a decentralized terminal coding agent designed for developers who want full ownership with no vendor lock-in. Free with BYO API keys. Features customizable keyboard shortcuts, Android Termux support, and atomic binary updates. No vision support or subagents. Smaller community. Best for privacy-focused developers who want full control over their coding agent.

name: OpenAI Codex
recommended: Parallel ticket processing and batch tasks
description: OpenAI Codex is a CLI and cloud-based coding agent with parallel Git worktree execution and cloud sandboxed agents. SWE-bench score of 72.8%. Included in ChatGPT Plus ($20-200/mo). Open source CLI but cloud-dependent for parallel mode. OpenAI models only with usage caps on Plus plan. Best for parallel ticket processing and batch tasks.

name: Goose
recommended: Extensible coding agent with MCP tool integration
description: Goose is an extensible open-source terminal coding agent with MCP (Model Context Protocol) support, written in Rust for performance. 51K+ GitHub stars. Free with BYO API keys and supports any LLM. No vision support, subagent system, or built-in cron. Best for developers wanting an extensible coding agent with MCP tool integration.

name: OpenClaw
recommended: Cross-platform AI assistant for daily tasks
description: OpenClaw is a cross-platform desktop AI assistant with vision support, ACP protocol support, cron scheduling, and background tasks. 382K+ GitHub stars. Free and open source. Desktop application (not terminal-based) requiring local installation. No native subagent system. Best for cross-platform personal AI assistant for daily tasks.

name: Codebuff
pros: Terminal-native code generation with zero IDE dependencies
Multi-model support (Claude, GPT-4, local models via Ollama)
Supports custom system prompts and personas
cons: No subagent delegation or cron scheduling
Limited IDE integration (no VS Code extension)
recommended: Developers who want a lightweight, terminal-first coding agent for quick code generation tasks without IDE overhead — great for SSH sessions, containers, and minimal environments.
description: Codebuff is a free, open-source terminal coding agent that uses BYO API keys (supports Anthropic, OpenAI, and local models via Ollama). It focuses on fast, clean code generation with a distraction-free terminal interface — no IDE, no bloat, just code. At ~7K GitHub stars, it's a lightweight alternative to heavier agents like Cline or OpenCode. Key features: multi-model support with automatic model selection, git-aware repository context reading, custom system prompts, and zero telemetry. The agent reads your codebase, understands the task, and writes code directly to files. No plugin system, no subagents, no cron — it's deliberately minimal. Best for: quick terminal-based code generation, SSH/remote development, container environments, and developers who prefer a no-frills CLI over an IDE extension. MIT licensed, actively maintained, Node.js-based.

name: AmpCode
bestFor: Unconstrained agentic coding with multi-model routing
pros: Multi-model routing (auto-selects best model per task)
Unconstrained token usage — no hard caps
Built-in code review with diff analysis
Full git integration with PR workflows
cons: Free tier closed to new signups (waitlist)
recommended: Teams and developers who want maximum agentic capability with flexible billing — ideal for complex multi-file refactors where you need the best model per subtask.
description: AmpCode is a terminal and web-based coding agent with pay-as-you-go pricing (historical free tier ~$10/day credits, currently waitlisted). It offers unconstrained agentic coding with intelligent multi-model routing — automatically selecting the best model (Claude, GPT-4, others) for each subtask. Key differentiators: subagent delegation for parallel execution, built-in code review with diff analysis, team thread sharing, and background task execution. The agent can break down complex tasks, spawn subagents, and synthesize results. Full git integration with PR creation and review workflows. Plugin system allows custom skills and workflows. Closed source, cloud-dependent, no flat subscription. Best for: teams needing maximum capability with variable billing, complex refactors requiring multi-model intelligence, and collaborative agentic workflows. Note: free tier access is limited; check ampcode.com for current availability.

name: GitHub Copilot CLI
bestFor: GitHub-native terminal agent with PR/issue integration
recommended: Developers in GitHub ecosystem wanting terminal agent
description: GitHub Copilot CLI is GitHub's terminal coding agent, available with a Copilot subscription ($10-39/mo). It integrates natively with GitHub's ecosystem, including PR creation, issue linking, and repository context. Supports multi-model (Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5), has built-in MCP server, and a fleet of parallel subagents. Requires Copilot subscription; GitHub ecosystem dependent with premium request quota limits.

name: Cline CLI
description: Cline CLI is a free, open-source terminal coding agent with autonomous coding and browser automation capabilities. 64K+ GitHub stars. It uses BYO API keys and can interact with the browser, run terminal commands, and create/edit files autonomously. Features MCP integration and multi-provider support. No cron or subagents. Resource-heavy. Best for autonomous coding with browser automation.

name: Kimi CLI
bestFor: Moonshot AI's CLI coding agent with skills & MCP
pros: 9K+ GitHub stars, backed by Moonshot AI
Skills system for repeatable coding workflows
Git-aware with diff and commit helpers
recommended: Developers wanting Moonshot Kimi integration with skills/MCP workflows — especially strong for Chinese-language codebases and Moonshot ecosystem users.
description: Kimi CLI is Moonshot AI's free terminal coding agent with BYO API key support. At 9K+ GitHub stars, it's a well-maintained open-source agent (Apache-2.0) offering strong code generation and reasoning capabilities with access to Moonshot's Kimi models. Key differentiators: a Skills system for defining repeatable coding workflows (similar to OpenCode's SKILL.md), full MCP support for tool integration, and ACP protocol for IDE integration (VS Code, JetBrains). Multi-provider support means you can use Kimi models or any OpenAI-compatible API. Git integration includes diff viewing, commit message generation, and branch management. No vision, cron, subagents, or background tasks — it's a focused, single-agent terminal tool. Best for: developers in the Moonshot ecosystem, Chinese-language codebases (Kimi excels at Chinese), and teams wanting skills/MCP workflows without OpenCode's complexity. Single binary install, Node.js-based, actively maintained by MoonshotAI.

name: Groq Code CLI
bestFor: Instant iteration with Groq's ultra-fast LPU inference
pros: Ultra-fast inference via Groq LPU (~100+ tokens/sec)
Supports Llama, Mixtral, Gemma via Groq
cons: Groq API models only (no Anthropic/OpenAI direct)
Requires Groq API key (free tier available)
recommended: Developers who prioritize raw iteration speed above all — fastest token generation for rapid code/edit cycles.
description: Groq Code CLI is a free, open-source terminal coding agent powered by Groq's ultra-fast LPU (Language Processing Unit) inference, delivering 100+ tokens/second for near-instant code generation. At 737 GitHub stars, it's a lightweight (~5MB single binary) MIT-licensed tool focused on speed above all else. Uses BYO Groq API keys (free tier: 14,400 requests/day) and supports Llama 3, Mixtral, Gemma, and other models hosted on Groq. Key features: plugin system for custom workflows, git integration with diff viewing and commit helpers, custom system prompts, and fully local-first operation with zero telemetry. No multi-provider support (Groq models only), no vision, no cron, no subagents, no background tasks — it's a specialized speed tool. Best for: developers who need the fastest possible iteration cycles, rapid prototyping, and high-volume code generation where latency matters. Groq's free tier is generous for individual use. Actively maintained by the build-with-groq community.

name: Grok Build CLI
bestFor: xAI's coding agent with parallel Society of Mind architecture
pros: 8 parallel agents via Society of Mind architecture
recommended: xAI subscribers wanting maximum parallel execution — 8 agents working simultaneously on different parts of a codebase.
description: Grok Build CLI is xAI's free coding agent for xAI subscribers. At 13K+ GitHub stars (Apache-2.0), it features a unique Society of Mind architecture that spawns up to 8 parallel subagents to work on different parts of a codebase simultaneously — file edits, tests, docs, and research all running concurrently. Key differentiators: vision support for image/code screenshot analysis, fullscreen TUI with rich markdown/code rendering, subagent delegation, background tasks, and a plugin system. Git integration includes diff viewing, commit generation, and PR creation. Requires xAI subscription (Grok models only, no BYO keys), no cron scheduling, Linux/macOS native (Windows via WSL). Newer platform with growing but smaller community vs Cline/OpenCode. Best for: xAI ecosystem developers who want maximum parallel throughput on complex multi-file tasks — refactors, test generation, and documentation can run across 8 agents at once. Actively developed by xAI-org.
